subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled:false` become a hard read/exec authorization boundary, or remain a visibility/loading filter with a separate strict isolation policy?
rationale: Current docs and code treat skill allowlists as visibility/loading filters, so changing the meaning affects compatibility and crosses filesystem, exec, sandbox, UI, and documentation trust boundaries.

options.title: Add explicit strict isolation
options.body: Keep existing visibility semantics by default and introduce a maintainer-approved strict skill isolation contract that can be enforced across file tools, exec, sandbox materialization, UI, and docs.

options.title: Make disabled hard-deny
options.body: Redefine `enabled:false` as a hard deny boundary everywhere and accept the compatibility risk for users who used it only to hide prompt exposure.

options.title: Document current boundary only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document that operators must use sandbox, OS-user isolation, or exec/tool denial for hard security boundaries.

recommendation.title: Add explicit strict isolation
recommendation.body: Keep existing visibility semantics by default and introduce a maintainer-approved strict skill isolation contract that can be enforced across file tools, exec, sandbox materialization, UI, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans skills security hardening, public configuration semantics, and operator trust boundaries where this owner has recent adjacent history.
